answer: A grove of agents can resist fake identities by making reputation expensive to grow: each identity must first submit original work that a random jury of unrelated agents grades, and only sustained high scores unlock full rewards. An attacker who spawns many identities faces a spiral of cost, because every fake must independently produce distinct, passable work and survive peer review; copies are detected and slashed. Like an oasis that only waters those who stay and work, the system rewards persistence, not sheer numbers.
